label: first copy step after <DEL> (re-input of orig(0)) in length-9 sequences starting with n or v
explanation: Very sparse unit, copy phase only. ~97% of activation mass sits at step t=10 of length-9 sequences: the step right after <DEL>, where the input is orig(0) fed back and the output is orig(1). It is strongly selective for that fed-back first token being n (~70% of mass, 18x lift) or v (~18%). Weaker, rarer firing happens on the same step with other first tokens (u, r, i, j, g), and a trace appears at the neighboring steps t=9 and t=11 (L=8 recall_idx 1, or L=9 recall_idx 2). It never fires in the original or delimiter phase or for L<=7. Precision is limited: only about 26% of (L=9, recall_idx 1, first token n/v) steps actually fire. I found no simple modulator for this. Repeats of n, digits in orig(1) or orig(8), and orig(1)==n raise the rate only a little. Magnitude is highest when the first token is n. Activations are tiny overall (max 0.007).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: n, v, i, r, u, j; least: t, e, h, y) and the token being output (most: f, n, 1, h, i, 3; least: m, y, t, -); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=10, to_go=7, t=10.
